ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, statutory officers and clients against the Luxembourg FIU lists, OFAC SDN list, UN Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and a commercial PEP database. Enhanced due diligence applies to PEPs, their family members and close associates, and to high-risk third-country residents. Ongoing transaction monitoring and annual periodic re-screening are required under the AML/CFT Law and CSSF Regulation 12-02.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – lbr.lu; RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be written in Latin script and may be registered in one of the official administrative languages (French, German, Luxembourgish) or transliterated with an official-language version filed for the RCS index. The legal-form suffix 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL' is mandatory and must correspond to the entity type. Names must be distinctive, not misleading, and consistent with ISIC/NACE activity declarations for executive search/headhunting.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Luxembourg / Luxembourgeois (when implying official or state status)
SARL (when not the exact legal form)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within one month of a written rejection by the RCS, the applicant may file an administrative appeal before the Registrar of the RCS, attaching the refusal letter, name reservation receipt and corrected alternatives. If the Registrar maintains the refusal, a judicial appeal may be brought before the Administrative Tribunal within three months of notification. For names containing sensitive tokens, a prior ministerial/CSSF opinion should be obtained before filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is accepted only when provided by a licensed domiciliation agent and is not, by itself, sufficient to establish commercial substance. For ISIC 7830 executive-search/headhunting, the tax and AML authorities require local management, operational decision-making, physical premises or controlled workspace, and employees/agents sufficient to support invoicing, client relationships and payroll.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 10-15% annual probability for a standard low-risk SARL with timely filings; increases above 50% if RBE/UBO inconsistencies, AML suspicious-transaction reports, or insufficient-substance criteria are triggered.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Sections 1, 4, 101, 102, 110, and 113-1 regarding SARL formation, capital, and governance)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies (Luxembourg Business Registers, LBR)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation and coordinated articles of association filed for registration with the LBR
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital of EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and paid up in cash at incorporation; if registered office is placed in a building owned by the company, additional valuation and special auditor requirements apply; share capital is notarially escrowed until registration is completed
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the incorporators' subscription of the full share capital be and is hereby ratified; RESOLVED that the registered office of the Société à Responsabilité Limitée be and is hereby fixed at Luxembourg City, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; RESOLVED that the directors nominated are appointed as managers for the first period of office with full authority to open bank accounts, sign mandates, and complete statutory filings; RESOLVED that the articles of association, as executed before the notary, are approved; RESOLVED that the managers are authorized to obtain tax, social security, and other business registrations. Adoption by unanimous vote.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial execution and signature of articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary appointed within Luxembourg (Chambre des Notaires du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare draft articles of association in French or German; submit identification documents, proof of address, and capital subscription statements to the notary; notary verifies identity, capacity, and legality of the object; sign the notarized deed of incorporation in person or by valid power of attorney.
required_dossiers: Passport or EU identity card of each shareholder and manager
Bank certificate of share capital deposit in escrow
Power of attorney if signed by proxy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises a query, cure by amending articles, clarifying ownership evidence, or providing updated capital deposit proof and resubmitting within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of share capital in escrow
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg bank or credit institution holding the escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary escrow account in the company's name; transfer at least EUR 12,000 of fully paid cash capital from shareholders; obtain a capital deposit certificate for inclusion in the notarial deed; release of funds only occurs after LBR registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional AML documentation, provide passport, proof of address, and source of wealth; any delay in deposit extends the notarial execution date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication and registration at the LBR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarial deed, articles of association, and complete registration request electronically through the LBR portal; pay filing fees; LBR verifies compatibility of the corporate object with legal activities and assigns the registration number.
required_dossiers: Identification of managers and authorized signatories
Statement of subscription and paid-up capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the LBR queries any mandatory disclosure or capacity issue, supplement the filing with corrected certificates or amended notarial declarations within two business days; if rejected, restart via a rectificatory notarial deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration and social security formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) and Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the national business number (matricule) and corporate income tax/TVA identification; register as an employer with CCSS if hiring staff; complete the commercial register extract collection from LBR; provide the registered office certificate to the tax administration.
required_dossiers: Lease or ownership proof of registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is delayed, verify the LBR extract date and resubmit with updated documents; for CCSS refusal, present corrected payroll registration forms and employment contracts.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emission thresholds apply; obligations limited to general waste separation, electronics take-back compliance, and data privacy physical records handling per Luxembourg waste and GDPR rules

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the municipal fire brigade; structural load clearance for office premises from the Administration des bâtiments publics; workplace health and safety inspection by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM)

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Grand Duchy of Luxembourg — Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) is the competent VAT and indirect-tax authority; Administration des contributions directes (ACD) is the competent direct-tax authority; unified business e-government portals: MyGuichet.lu, guichet.lu and the secure business space (Espace sécurisé des entreprises / SSE), with AEDT electronic filing module eTVA and ACD eCDF portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Resident SARL: upon incorporation, the company automatically receives its national business registration number (matricule) from the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) via the RCS; this matricule is the statutory TIN for corporate income tax, municipal business tax, net wealth tax, and social-security reporting. For VAT, the SARL must apply with the AEDT through MyGuichet.lu using the electronic VAT identification form within 15 days of commencing taxable supplies; the VAT number is issued as LU followed by 8 digits. Foreign entities: an EU-established business with Luxembourg taxable supplies — for which there is no turnover threshold — registers directly with the AEDT or uses the EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS) where the transaction qualifies. A non-EU-established business without a Luxembourg establishment must appoint an AEDT-approved Luxembourg VAT representative (mandataire TVA) and file a registration request together with certified evidence of home-country TIN and commercial registration, EORI data for goods transactions, authenticated identification of directors/members, and a power of attorney; the entire procedure is paperless and does not involve a US-style TIN application.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the Luxembourg SARL is a per se opaque and fully taxable capital company resident in Luxembourg; it is subject to corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités), municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) and, generally, net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune) on worldwide income, with treaty relief, EU Directive relief and the participation-exemption regime; no pass-through or transparent classification is available at national level.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists; the SARL cannot elect transparent treatment. Available statutory elections and regimes: (a) tax unity for CIT under Art. 164bis LIR between a resident parent and resident subsidiaries held directly or indirectly at least 90%, with identical fiscal year-end, effective for an irrevocable 5-year block; (b) VAT grouping (assujetti unique, Art. 60 VAT Law), including one-person VAT grouping; (c) small-business VAT exemption election under Art. 57 VAT Law where annual taxable turnover does not exceed EUR 30,000; (d) VAT option (assujettissement) for real-estate leasing and certain financial services under Art. 48 VAT Law; (e) participation-exemption regime for dividend and realised capital-gain income from qualifying shareholdings (at least 10% or, for dividend purposes, an acquisition price of at least EUR 1.2 million) held continuously for at least 12 months, subject to Art. 166/166bis LIR conditions; (f) ATAD 1/2 hybrid-mismatch rules apply mandatorily — no domestic election is available; (g) Pillar Two qualified domestic minimum top-up tax and international top-up tax apply from fiscal year 2024 to groups with consolidated revenue of EUR 750 million or more.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the Eurosystem and coordinated with the European Central Bank (ECB); prudential banking supervision and AML/CFT oversight are jointly discharged by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) and the BCL, with residual competence over EU/UN sanctions implementation and counter-terrorism financing measures reserved to the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment:
Luxembourg maintains full euro convertibility and a completely liberalised cross-border payments environment; there are no exchange controls, no prior authorisation requirements, and no distinction in practical treatment between current-account transactions (retainer fees, contractor settlements, intercompany service charges) and capital-account transactions (equity injections, share redemptions, liquidation distributions, loan repayments), consistent with TFEU Articles 63-65, the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements, and the BCL/CSSF statistical reporting frame.
Profit-remittance hurdles are exclusively fiscal rather than exchange-control in nature: (i) dividends distributed by a Luxembourg SARL are subject to a 15% domestic withholding tax, reducible to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (qualifying parent holding at least 10% for an uninterrupted 12-month period) or to lower treaty rates (commonly 5%); (ii) the underlying profit bears standard corporate income tax of 17%, municipal business tax of approximately 6.75% to 8.4% on the taxable profit of service companies, and a 0.5% net-wealth tax on net assets above the statutory threshold; and (iii) no waiting period, conversion obligation, or central-bank consent applies to the remittance itself, which can be executed immediately upon dividend payment approval by the shareholders' meeting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Luxembourg imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender, forced repatriation timeline, or mandatory conversion ratio for services exports, including executive-search and headhunting receipts. Retainer and success-fee invoices may be denominated and collected in EUR, USD, GBP, or any freely convertible currency; the SARL may retain balances onshore or offshore at its sole commercial discretion. The only administrative duty is indirect: the resident receiving bank captures cross-border credits for BCL balance-of-payments statistics (transactions in excess of the EUR 12,500 aggregation threshold are declared in the bank's BCL filings), and no corporate notification is required.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability:
Conditional-High as an ancillary payment rail; Medium as a primary treasury bank. The payload-mandated rail of Wise B2B (operated for EEA clients by Wise Europe SA, an e-money institution licensed under PSD2 and passporting into Luxembourg) is legally viable for retainer collections, vendor disbursements, and contractor settlements, including euro IBANs executed over SEPA and SWIFT-compatible non-EUR corridors.
Material constraints: (i) the statutory share-capital deposit must be evidenced by a blocked-account certificate issued by a Luxembourg credit institution, which no EMI can provide; (ii) BCL-reporting-grade corporate liquidity, multi-currency cash pooling, netting, documentary credits, and FX lines require a domestic banking relationship; (iii) tax payments to the Administration des Contributions Directes and social-security contributions to the CSSF (Centre Commun de la Securite Sociale) are operationally segregated onto domestic SEPA accounts in practice; and (iv) EMI balances are not covered by the Luxembourg deposit-guarantee scheme, imposing counterparty concentration risk above EUR 100,000. The recommended treasury topology is therefore a dual-rail structure: a domestic house bank for settlement and regulatory-grade liquidity, with Wise B2B optimising low-value, high-frequency cross-border retainer flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand:
Physical presence is the default mandate for the SARL's manager (gerant) and, in most institutions, for the majority ultimate beneficial owner. Luxembourg banks subject to the Law of 12 November 2004 on AML/CTF and CSSF Regulation 12-02, as amended, require in-person identification at onboarding unless the bank has deployed a CSSF-approved remote electronic identity solution and the client is classified low-risk.
Remote opening is increasingly tolerated for low-risk professional clients where: (a) the SARL holds a Luxembourg registered office and a valid RCS excerpt; (b) at least one gerant appears physically at a Luxembourg branch; and (c) all non-resident UBOs deliver notarially certified and, where applicable, apostilled/legalised passports, proof of residential address, and a certified copy of the notarial incorporation deed. National eID cards of EEA residents can be verified via video for supplementary signatories in certain banks. Practical planning assumption: one Luxembourg in-person visit for the gerant and primary UBO, with the balance of the ownership chain onboarding via videoconference supported by an approved fiduciary or Luxembourg law-firm cover letter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO chain opacity: the SARL's ownership is intermediated by trusts, foundations, or entities resident in non-transparent jurisdictions such that natural-person owners cannot be identified at the 25% threshold.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete organisational chart from the SARL to each natural-person UBO (disclosing every 5%-plus direct or indirect holding and confirming the 25%-plus one statutory threshold); notarially certified passports of all UBOs; source-of-wealth evidence (three years of tax assessments, audited parent financials, share-purchase contracts, inheritance deeds); a signed UBO declaration filed with the Luxembourg RCS; and an opinion letter from a Luxembourg law firm or CSSF-licensed fiduciary confirming the absence of bearer shares and nominee concealment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PEP, adverse-media, or sanctions screening hits against the gerant, UBO, or an invoicing counterparty (including retainer-source clients in high-risk sectors or jurisdictions).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed PEP-status disclosure forms; substance-driven source-of-funds evidence for the initial capital and forecast retainer deposits; genuine commercial underliers (signed retainer agreements, engagement letters, and ISIC 7830/NACE 78.30-consistent contracts); negative sanction-screen outputs from an approved provider (World-Check, Dow Jones, or EU Consolidated List screening) dated within 90 days; and the SARL's written acceptance of enhanced ongoing monitoring and transaction-review thresholds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Letterbox-company pattern: a domiciliation-service address with no demonstrable operational footprint, payroll, or decision-making substance in Luxembourg.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Standard commercial domiciliation agreement with a licensed fiduciary; fixed-term lease or sub-lease plus telecommunications and data-services contracts evidencing office substance; the SARL's business plan, headcount budget, and revenue forecast; CCSS registrations for employees and statutory accidents-insurance filings; and a management-services agreement evidencing the Luxembourg gerant's binding decision-making authority over retainer pricing, candidate placement, and treasury.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital-contribution fungibility risk: the statutory minimum share capital is wired from a third-party lender, a cryptocurrency exchange, or an unvetted non-EEA bank, obscuring the origin of funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised deed of subscription and full-payment statement identifying each subscriber; blocked-account certificate (attestation de blocage) issued by the receiving Luxembourg credit institution; the full inbound wire trail (SWIFT MT103 or SEPA remittance showing subscriber name, source IBAN, and payment purpose identified as equity capital contribution); the remitter's own bank statements; executed loan or shareholder-contribution agreements if the funds are intra-group; and board minutes approving the capitalisation and confirming non-reliance on third-party deposits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Activity-perimeter ambiguity: the bank reclassifies ISIC 7830 executive search as regulated employment or temporary-work intermediation, triggering a different licensing regime and escalated AML/KYC treatment.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RCS excerpt and articles of association narrowly confining the corporate object to C-suite executive search, headhunting, and specialist-tech talent advisory; client and candidate contracts expressly excluding payroll outsourcing, employer-of-record services, and temporary-staffing intermediation; CCSS and ACD registrations proving no employee-payroll scale-in is performed; the commercial billing model (fixed retainer plus success fee, never acting as employer of record); and written confirmation from the competent Ministry of Labour authority that no temporary-work-agency licence is triggered by pure headhunting activity.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inward-capital injection protocol: (1) the statutory minimum share capital of the SARL is subscribed before a Luxembourg notary and deposited in the SARL's name into a blocked account (compte bloque) held at a BCL-member credit institution; the notary obtains the depositary's blocked-funds certificate (attestation de blocage) and will not execute the deed absent receipt thereof; (2) upon RCS registration, the blocked balance is released into the operational account by internal book transfer; (3) subsequent cross-border injections from a parent or UBO are routed via SWIFT MT103 (USD/GBP/CHF) or SEPA Credit Transfer (EUR) to the receiving account's IBAN/BIC, with the remittance narrative quoting the corporate objective and legal basis, e.g., 'capital increase pursuant to notarial deed dated [date]' and using the bank-prescribed ISO 20022 purpose code 'SUPP' (supplementary paid-in capital) or 'COMC' for shareholder current-account advances; (4) the receiving bank verifies the notarial deed, the RCS excerpt, the UBO declaration, and the origin-of-funds source statement, and files the inbound direct investment into the BCL balance-of-payments statistics system under the direct-investment equity-capital category; no prior BCL or CSSF authorisation is required; (5) for USD or GBP wires without a pre-existing corresponding-bank routing, the SARL should pre-notify the relationship manager 48 hours in advance to avoid a compliance hold pending remitter-name screening and purpose-code validation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing-rail matrix for the headhunting treasury: (i) SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) and SEPA Instant (SCT Inst) for all euro-denominated payments to EEA counterparties, including retainer refunds, contractor commissions, and settlement of success fees, providing TARGET2 finality; (ii) SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA and non-euro disbursements (USD, GBP, CHF, and Asia-Pacific corridors), with field 70 remittance information quoting the retainer or invoice number for reconciliation; (iii) domestic SEPA Credit Transfers to the Administration des Contributions Directes (taxes) and the CCSS (social security) dedicated IBANs; (iv) internal book transfers for blocked-account release at incorporation; (v) documentary instruments — commercial letters of credit are materially inapposite to executive-search receivables, but where a foreign client demands bank payment undertakings, a standby letter of credit (SBLC) or bank counter-guarantee can be opened through the Luxembourg house bank, with the economic default collection rail remaining SWIFT MT103 or SEPA; and (vi) Wise B2B as a low-cost secondary rail for high-frequency, low-value retainer disbursements and contractor payments, subject to the EMI counterparty and balance-guarantee limitations previously described. Standing instruction: maintain a liquidity buffer of at least two months of operating costs in the BCL-member operating account to avoid overdraft triggers and negative-interest carry.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable vanilla FX forwards in EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and EUR/CHF, executed bilaterally under ISDA/CSA documentation or through the house bank's FX prime desk, limited to forecast retainer and success-fee flows and strictly non-speculative in corporate intent

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted-currency exposures (CNY, INR, BRL) where retainer contracts are invoiced in EUR or USD but the ultimate candidate or client economics are settled in restricted currencies; the NDF is cash-settled in EUR or USD against the market fixing without requiring onshore deliverability

Plain-vanilla cross-currency swaps and FX swaps converting USD- or GBP-denominated retainer surpluses into euro working capital and vice versa, with tenors aligned to the invoicing cycle and board-approved counterparty limits

Long-only FX options (purchased puts and calls) and zero-premium collar/range-forward structures combining a purchased out-of-the-money option with a sold offsetting option, eligible for cash-flow hedge designation under IFRS 9 where the underlying exposure is highly probable forecast revenue

Spot FX conversions and same-day rolling one-week forwards for treasury liquidity balancing, executed only through approved counterparties and recorded under the SARL's written FX policy to preserve hedge-accounting documentation and internal-control integrity

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory accounts (balance sheet, profit and loss account, notes) and, if required, the management report of the SARL
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: RCS – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (Luxembourg Business Registers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within eight months after the balance-sheet date; for a 31 December fiscal year the deposit is due by 31 August of the subsequent year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors exposed to a fine up to €5,000 and coercive court order (astreinte) to deposit; the RCS may ultimately strike the company off the register if annual accounts remain outstanding.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax (IRC) and net wealth tax (IFT) declarations, including income and net wealth computations, schedules and appendices
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally due on or before 31 December of the year following the tax year for calendar-year taxpayers; non-calendar fiscal year ends follow the anniversary of the balance sheet date with possible extension via e-Tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing interest at 0.6% per month, late-payment interest, penalties up to 10% of the tax arrears, and possible administrative lump-sum assessment; persistent non-filing can trigger criminal sanctions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal) declaration — filed with and annexed to the CIT return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same deadline and extension regime as the CIT/NWT declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Liability to municipal late-payment surcharges, penal interest at 0.6% per month, and enforcement procedure through the tax collector.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial-owner data and immediate statement of any change in direct or indirect ownership structure, with substantiation documents
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) – Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Once per calendar year (no later than 31 December); amendments within one month of the applicable ownership change or transfer of shares
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to €2,000; in severe cases criminal penalties up to €1 million for legal entities plus imprisonment of directors; false declarations trigger higher penalties.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Luxembourg SARL must appoint an independent auditor (cabinet de révision) if it exceeds at least two of three criteria on its balance-sheet date: (1) total balance sheet exceeding €4.4 million; (2) net turnover (exclusive of VAT) exceeding €8.8 million; (3) average headcount exceeding 50. Executive-search headhunting SARLs below these thresholds remain exempt unless required by shareholders, the Articles of Association, or a parent undertaking's audit group requirements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg generally accepted accounting principles (Lux GAAP) under the Law of 19 December 2002 on the accounting records and annual accounts of undertakings; EU-endorsed IFRS is permitted for consolidated and certain standalone reporting but is not typically mandatory for a standalone SARL.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each Luxembourg SARL must file with the RBE (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) precise beneficial-owner information and undertake an annual confirmation (actualisation) of that data no later than 31 December of each calendar year. Any share transfer or change in ownership/control rights must be declared within one month of the transaction. The Public Prosecutor and certain regulatory authorities have access, and directors are personally liable for false or missing declarations.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% corporate income tax (CIT) on taxable income exceeding EUR 175,000; 15% on the first EUR 175,000; plus a 7% solidarity surcharge on the CIT and municipal business tax (communal trade tax) at a nominal base rate of 3% multiplied by the communal coefficient (225% in Luxembourg City, i.e., 6.75%). Aggregate CIT plus solidarity and municipal business tax burden for a profitable Luxembourg City SARL is approximately 24.94%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption: 100% exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains (10% shareholding or acquisition price above EUR 1.2 million for dividends and EUR 6 million for gains, 12-month holding period). IP box regime: 80% exemption of net qualifying IP income, yielding an effective rate of approximately 5.19% on IP income. R&D tax credit: 20% of qualifying in-house R&D expenditure (13% for subcontracted R&D to approved research bodies). Unlimited loss carryforward for losses realized from tax year 2017. Municipal business tax is deductible for CIT purposes.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory time limit for losses incurred as of tax year 2017; losses from earlier years were subject to a 17-year carryforward limit); no carryback permitted.
